# Overview

[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/github-pytifex-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/benedekaibas/pytifex)
[![Python 3.12+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](https://github.com/benedekaibas/pytifex-demo/blob/main/LICENSE)

Pytifex automatically discovers disagreements between Python type checkers by mining real bugs from type checker repositories, generating targeted test cases with an LLM, and establishing ground truth through multi-phase evaluation.

## What `uv run pytifex` actually does, in order

**1. Mine seeds** — once, up front, unless `--no-github`. Pulls closed, confirmed bug-fix issues straight from GitHub:

```python
# github_issues.py
def is_confirmed_bug(issue: dict) -> bool:
    if issue.get("state") != "closed":
        return False
    if issue.get("state_reason") == "not_planned":
        return False
    return True
```

**2. Generate** — a batch of new code gets written by the LLM, seeded from those issues (or from the built-in patterns if there are no seeds):

```python
# pipeline.py
if seed_examples:
    prompt = build_seed_based_prompt(batch_seeds, batch_size)
else:
    prompt = build_expert_prompt(batch_size)
```

**3. Check** — every generated example runs through mypy, pyrefly, zuban, and ty.

**4. Filter** — a disagreement is any example where the checkers don't all return the same status:

```python
# pipeline.py
def has_disagreement(results: dict[str, CheckerResult]) -> bool:
    statuses = [r.status for r in results.values()]
    return len(set(statuses)) > 1
```

Disagreements get kept as-is. Examples where all four checkers agreed get one shot at a fix: sent back to the LLM with the real checker output attached, up to `--max-refinements` times. Steps 2–4 repeat in batches until `--num-examples` disagreements are found, or `--max-attempts` runs out.

**5. Evaluate** — everything that survived gets saved to `generated_examples/<timestamp>/`, then run through two phases: Phase 1 checks whether the code crashes at runtime, Phase 2 fuzzes it with Hypothesis-generated, type-conformant inputs. Whichever phase finds concrete proof decides which checker was right. If neither does, an LLM judge gets the final say.

A verdict is never guessed upfront — it only gets issued once there's an actual crash or an actual successful run behind it.

## Type checkers tested

| Checker | Version |
|---------|---------|
| [mypy](https://github.com/python/mypy) | 1.19.0 |
| [pyrefly](https://github.com/facebook/pyrefly) | 0.44.2 |
| [zuban](https://pypi.org/project/zuban/) | 0.3.0 |
| [ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty) | 0.0.1-alpha.32 |

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/benedekaibas/pytifex
cd pytifex

export COHERE_API_KEY=your_key

uv run --extra dev pytifex --model command-a-03-2025
```

`--extra dev` is what pulls in mypy, pyrefly, zuban, and ty — they're an optional dependency group in `pyproject.toml`, not a base dependency, so a plain `uv run pytifex` won't install them.

> Pytifex is a research tool I built for a senior comprehensive project. The idea is to find type checker bugs proactively, before a user runs into them in production.
